children: BT Group shares advanced after the company reported higher profit for the first half of fiscal 2027, when it cut 11% of its workforce, slowed the rate of broadband line losses and added customers for its high-speed fiber service.
Shares were up 5.5% at 244.30 pence during morning trading on Thursday.

The British telecommunications company said net profit increased to 809 million pounds ($1.09 billion) in the six months to the end of September, from 651 million pounds a year ago. Revenue edged up 0.6% to 8.75 billion pounds.

BT said its transformation program remains on track to deliver 3.5 billion pounds of gross annualized cost savings by fiscal 2030. In the first six months of the year, the company made 312 million pounds of savings. BT cut its total workforce by 11% to 90,000 staff during the period.
BT is trying to reduce costs and stem customer declines amid increased competition, as it invests in the rollout of high-speed internet access.
The company added 1.1 million Openreach fiber customers in the period, bringing its take-up rate to 41%.

Openreach broadband line losses were down 175,000 in the second quarter, slowing from a 192,000 fall in the first quarter. The company maintained its guidance for an 800,000 drop in fiscal 2027, but Bernstein analysts said there is potential upside to this after the rate of losses slowed.

BT backed its guidance for the year, including for adjusted revenue between 17.1 billion pounds and 17.6 billion pounds, and for normalized free cash flow of around 2.0 billion pounds. The company still expects normalized free cash flow to reach 3.0 billion pounds by the end of the decade.

"An expected fall in capital expenditure over the medium term as the fiber broadband network buildout completes will boost group cash flows, increasing financial flexibility and potentially enabling a paying down of debt or an increased dividend, or even both," Interactive Investor's Keith Bowman said.
BT raised its interim dividend to 2.50 pence per share from 2.45 pence a year ago.
